title: Recorded report server lifecycle
responsibility: Stores a server’s process identity and stops only the process matching that recorded identity.

inputs.name: stopReportServer.root
inputs.description: Store root used to locate `<root>/servers/<port>.json`; it determines which recorded server is considered for stopping. A file-read failure is treated as no record.

inputs.name: stopReportServer.port
inputs.description: Selects the `<port>.json` file under the store's `servers` directory and is copied to the result. The implementation stringifies it for the filename without checking network-port bounds.

inputs.name: processStarted.pid
inputs.description: PID passed to `ps` to query the process start time; the result is used to protect against signaling a reused PID. A failed or empty `ps` result becomes `undefined` rather than a rejection.

inputs.name: reportServerRecord.root
inputs.description: Root directory prefixed to the `servers/<port>.json` record path; it determines where the handle reads, writes and removes this record. The directory is created recursively only by `write()`, not by constructing the handle.

inputs.name: reportServerRecord.port
inputs.description: The number is interpolated into `<root>/servers/<port>.json` to select the record file. It is not checked against network-port bounds.

outputs.name: processStarted
outputs.description: The resolved value is the trimmed `ps -o lstart= -p <pid>` output for that PID, or `undefined` if `ps` fails or yields no text. It does not reserve or recheck the PID.

outputs.name: reportServerRecord
outputs.description: Returns a handle whose `file` is `<root>/servers/<port>.json` and whose methods read, write and remove that file. `read()` returns parsed JSON or `undefined` for read errors or empty content but rejects malformed JSON; `write()` creates parent directories and writes pretty JSON plus a newline, while `remove()` force-removes the file.

outputs.name: stopReportServer
outputs.description: The resolved result reports the requested port, whether PID and start time matched before signaling, and the recorded PID or a reason when available; no record yields `stopped: false` and a reason. A matching process receives SIGTERM, is polled for up to five seconds, then receives SIGKILL if still matched, and the record is removed on the normal path.

examples.reason: This report store recorded no server on this port.
The recorded server had already ended.

errors.name: SyntaxError
errors.description: Reading a nonempty record parses its contents with `JSON.parse` and does not catch parse failures, so malformed JSON rejects `read()` and `stopReportServer`.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: OS signal errors from `process.kill` and filesystem errors from `mkdir`, `writeFile` or `rm` propagate as Node errors; `stopReportServer` does not catch failed signals or record removal. `readFile` errors are caught and returned as absence.
